modules.intro: You wrote a prediction before this. Now you find out.
modules.title: Right Or Wrong, And What You Would Change
modules.aiNote: Ask what a fracture surface shows. Do not ask it to explain your break. You saw it.

blocks.content:
Upload a close photo of the break. Get the broken face in focus.

**Windows + Shift + S**, then **Ctrl + V** in an answer box.

You predicted a load and a place. Say plainly whether you were right. **A wrong prediction scores the same as a right one here** as long as you say which it was and why.

blocks.prompt: You predicted a load and a place it would break. What actually happened, and were you right about each one?
One change to this hook, and why. Name the place on the part.

blocks.content:
### Sources

- Hook Design and Manufacturing Guide, Where Hooks Break and Tournament Rules.
- Your own V3 prediction, your scale test, and the bracket board.
- Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design, 10th edition, Budynas and Nisbett, McGraw-Hill, 2015. Stress concentration and modes of failure.
- IDEA AI Use Policy.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: The broken face is visible and in focus and is this student's hook.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: A photograph where the break cannot be made out.

rubric.criterion: A close photograph of this student's own break

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: States clearly whether the predicted load and the predicted place were right. A stated miss is full marks.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Checks either the load or the place, not both.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Refers to the prediction without saying whether it held.

rubric.criterion: Compares the prediction to what happened, on both load and place

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Names the change, names where on the hook, and connects it to the break.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Names a change without connecting it to what actually broke.

rubric.criterion: Names one change and ties it to what the break showed

modules.intro: One slide in IDEA Hook Designs. This is what stays after the hooks are gone.
modules.title: Your Slide
modules.aiNote: No AI. These are your own images from your own work.

blocks.content:
Add one slide to **[IDEA Hook Designs](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1b6EarIaB3UGrG1Ee7HwFap8aBLAiEdwBRE6myKoFLg8/edit)**. Copy the layout of the slides already in there.

Six things have to be on it:

1. Your hook's name and your name.
2. The load it held, in pounds.
3. A CAD image of your hook.
4. Your simulation image, with the color scale showing.
5. A photo of the real printed hook.
6. A slicer view showing the toolpath.

You already have every one of these. The CAD, the simulation and the slicer view are on your own machine. The photo and the load come from today.

items: My slide is in the IDEA Hook Designs deck
Hook name and my name are on it
The load it held, in pounds
A CAD image and a simulation image with the color scale
A photo of the real printed hook

blocks.content:
### Sources

- [IDEA Hook Designs](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1b6EarIaB3UGrG1Ee7HwFap8aBLAiEdwBRE6myKoFLg8/edit), the slides already in the deck.
- Your own CAD, simulation, slicer and photographs.
- IDEA AI Use Policy.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Slide is in the deck with name, student, load, CAD, simulation and slicer view, and a photo of the real hook.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Slide is in the deck but one or two of the six are missing or unreadable.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: A slide exists with three or more of the six missing.

rubric.criterion: One slide in the deck carrying all six required things
